nodes.label: Folder Tree and Moves — Follow-Ups
nodes.rationale: The leftovers, ordered by what would hurt most to forget. None of it blocks a merge: every item is a known, written-down edge rather than a bug in what shipped.

nodes.label: repath_category Job (proposed, later refused)
nodes.rationale: Shaped like migrate_storage — resumable, one model directory at a time, an UPDATE per move so a crash costs one directory rather than the walk. The route enqueues; the worker walks. Re-pathing hundreds of directories is also not work an HTTP handler should hold open, and deploy.rs's RELOCATE_MODULE structurally forbids a folder handler from re-pathing a subtree.

nodes.label: The Descendant CTE Lives in the Page Query
nodes.rationale: The brief said implement it in PgFolders; it went inline into PgParts::page instead — one query rather than two round trips, and one descent implementation rather than two to keep in step. Settled as accepted after the merge, because splitting it now would create the second descent implementation the original note was worried about.

nodes.label: Two Tree Scale Ceilings
nodes.rationale: PgFolders::tree pairs every folder with each descendant in one recursive CTE — O(nodes x depth) rows, depth bounded at 16 — and the tree is fetched whole on every sidebar load by design, because a lazy tree costs a round trip per expand on the interaction that has to feel instant. Hundreds of categories is nothing; tens of thousands would want a materialised count or a closure table. Measure before rewriting.

nodes.label: GET /api/parts/{id}/moves Has No Consumer
nodes.rationale: It also answers [] for a part id that names nothing, which is the same answer as 'this part has never moved' — deliberate, because nothing acts differently on the two and telling them apart costs a query on every read of a legitimately empty history. If a history is ever shown, the 404 starts to matter and should be added at the same time.

nodes.label: No UI for Creating or Renaming a Category
nodes.rationale: The routes are built and server-tested with no web consumer. Create depends on nothing and is the smallest real feature; rename needs prose create does not, because the directory keeps its original name and a person who renames Terain to Terrain will otherwise go looking for the fixed spelling. A PATCH carrying both a new name and a new parent applies the move first and the rename second and answers 409 renamedAfterMove — a branch with no test because no client sends both fields.
